brainiac Growth Chart

How big is brainiac's brain?

brainiac is a small computer brain. It reads text and writes text back, like a person chatting on a phone with no camera and no microphone. It is not given answers in code. It learns from a teacher, the way a child does.

Below, each row is one thing a brain can do. The green dot shows where brainiac stands today, next to animals and children. The orange ring shows where the planned work aims. Tap a row name for the simple page about it. The pillars page shows how the parts fit together.

When each skill took a big stepHow this chart is made Only passed tests that belong to one skill count (778 now); 245 passed tests that belong to no single skill are left out. A skill gets a mark on any day when at least 2 of its tests passed, or on the day it first passed any test. Marked days next to each other join into one mark (59 marks now). A bigger mark means more passed tests; the color is the skill. Failed tests on those days show in the hover but never make a mark. Days with no finished test at all are shaded.

Each mark is a stretch of days when many tests for one thing the brain can do passed (bigger means more passed). Pick a view below; hovering a mark shows what changed.

One thin line per skill, with a dot or bar on the days many tests passed: the best view for seeing which skill moved when.

Counts passed cards only: 727 of the 778 passed cards that belong to a skill fall on the marked days. 245 passed cards that are not tied to one skill are left out. Skills with no passed card yet: #17, #19, #20, #21, #23, #24, #25, #26, #27, #28.

How a dot is placed: brainiac's spot is the highest step whose core test it passes on a measured board number. A test that is only built, or a flag that is on without a score, does not count. Animal and age steps are rough, from well-known animal and child studies; each page links its sources. Rows for vision, hearing and talking phases, smell and taste: all stay at none yet until a board number passes; KB-276 to KB-281 are filed in Backlog and nothing is built. Eating when hungry: where the chain stands

Still 0 own eats outside a teacher cue, so the eating chain is not converging yet. The live read found 0 eats because the reward weight started at zero; a pay phase (2021) also failed, because it never gets hungry enough; planting the weight by hand (2022) also gave 0 acts of any kind; the research card (2023) is parked for your call.

School subjects by grade

The same ladder, read as school. Each subject splits into branches. A shaded cell means the branch is taught at that level; the number in the first shaded cell is the grade where it begins (K is kindergarten, Col is college, Grad is research). Grades follow US Common Core and NGSS style curricula. Animal and age steps are rough. Tap a subject name for its own page.

brainiac has no score in any subject yet. It is a text-in, text-out brain at an early stage, so every subject below reads none yet. Nothing here is invented progress.

Level labels

Basic K-2Beginner 3-5Intermediate 6-8Advanced 9-12Expert College+

Darker shade = higher level. Basic is kindergarten to grade 2, beginner grades 3 to 5, intermediate grades 6 to 8, advanced grades 9 to 12, expert is college, graduate study and research.

Stories per school grade (52)

Curriculum gate (KB-1106, design started 2026-10-18): brainiac moves to the next grade only after it gets a passing grade on every story of its current grade. Claude Code writes each story's test and rubric once brainiac has that grade's prerequisite capabilities, and grades the answers on live brainiac. A failed story files a card with its goal and needs, updates this chart, and starts a Claude Code run on that card. The card passes only when a final re-test of the failed story passes the rubric. Status (offline chart): G0 locked: needs KB-1111; G1 locked: needs G0 not all PASS; G2 locked: needs G1 not all PASS, KB-204, KB-150, KB-170; G3 locked: needs G2 not all PASS, KB-1112; G4 locked: needs G3 not all PASS, KB-1113.

Stories brainiac reads, from brainiac/input/stories, one folder per school stage. Cards = brainiac cards whose text names that stage or one of its stories (search them in the card strip above).

C. Non-science: cultural and belief systems

Traditions people hold as culture or belief. Each is labeled non-science, with the reason it is not evidence-based. Grade shows how deep the knowing of the tradition goes.

Astrology

Animals No animal reads stars for meaning.

Non-science: cultural/belief system, not evidence-based.Why not science: In a double-blind test (Carlson, Nature 1985), astrologers could not match birth charts to people better than chance. No mechanism links star positions to character.
